7.3 Cost and Practical Considerations
contents.html_ja: 7.3 コストと実務上の考慮事項

contents.html: The relationship between covering arrays and randomly generated tests presents some interesting issues. Generating covering arrays for combinatorial tests is complex; it has been shown to be an NP-hard problem. But generating tests randomly is trivial. Thus for large problems, we can compare the cost and time of generating a covering array versus producing tests randomly, measuring their coverage (Chapter 6), then adding tests as needed to provide full combinatorial coverage. Notice the last column of Table 10. For 4 way tests, once the number of parameters exceeds roughly 20, random generation will cover 99% or more of 4-way combinations. If a problem requires tests for 100 parameters, for example, covering array generators may require hours or days, or may simply be unable to handle that many parameters, but random tests could be generated quickly and easily. This is an option that may be cost effective even for smaller problems, and should be kept in mind for test planning.
contents.html_ja: 被覆配列とランダム生成テストの関係には、興味深い論点がある。組合せテスト用の被覆配列の生成は複雑であり、NP困難な問題であることが示されている。一方、ランダムなテスト生成は容易である。したがって大規模な問題では、被覆配列を生成するコストと時間をランダムにテストを生成するコストと時間と比較し、網羅率を測定し（第6章）、完全な組合せ網羅率を得るため必要に応じてテストを追加できる。表10の最後の列に注目されたい。4-wayテストでは、パラメーター数がおよそ20を超えると、ランダム生成により4-way組合せの99%以上が網羅される。たとえば100個のパラメーターを要する問題では、被覆配列生成器が数時間または数日かかる、あるいはその数のパラメーターを扱えない場合もあるが、ランダムテストなら迅速かつ容易に生成できる。これは小規模な問題でも費用対効果の高い選択肢となる可能性があり、テスト計画で考慮すべきである。

contents.html: 7.4 Chapter Summary
contents.html_ja: 7.4 本章の要約

contents.html: 1. Existing research has shown either no difference (for some problems) or higher failure detection effectiveness (for most problems) for combinatorial testing. Analyzing random test sets suggests a number of reasons for this result. In particular, a highly optimized t-way covering array may include fewer \(t+1\), \(t+2\), and higher degree interaction tests than an equivalent sized random test set. Similarly, a covering array algorithm that produces a larger, sub-optimal array may provide better failure detection because the larger array is statistically more likely to include \(t+1\), \(t+2\), and higher degree interaction tests as a byproduct of the test generation.
contents.html_ja: 1. 既存の研究は、組合せテストについて、（一部の問題では）差がないこと、または（大半の問題では）障害検出の有効性がより高いことを示している。ランダムテスト集合を分析すると、この結果の理由がいくつか示唆される。特に、高度に最適化されたt-way被覆配列は、同等の大きさのランダムテスト集合に比べて、\(t+1\)、\(t+2\)、およびそれより高い次数の相互作用のテストを少ししか含まないことがある。同様に、より大きく最適でない配列を生成する被覆配列アルゴリズムの方が、障害検出に優れることがある。配列が大きいほど、テスト生成の副産物として\(t+1\)、\(t+2\)、およびそれより高い次数の相互作用のテストを含む可能性が統計的に高くなるからである。

math_reconstruction.restorer_notes: 原本では「highly optimized t-way covering array」のtが立体で印字されているため、数式にせず本文のままとした（t+1、t+2のtは斜体）。

contents.html: 2. While the analysis reported here does not indicate that combinatorial testing is uniformly better than random, it does support a preference for combinatorial methods if the cost of applying the two test approaches is the same. This preference may be particularly relevant if the SUT is likely to contain multiple failures (as is usually the case). Single failures that depend on the interaction of two or more variables have a high likelihood of being detected by random tests, because the random test set may cover a high percentage of all \(t\)-way combinations. But the probability of detecting multiple failures declines rapidly as \(c^m\), for \(c =\) percent coverage and \(m =\) number of independent failures.
contents.html_ja: 2. ここで報告した分析は、組合せテストがランダムテストより一様に優れていることを示すものではないが、二つのテスト手法を適用するコストが同じであれば、組合せ手法を選ぶことを支持する。この選好は、SUTが複数の障害を含む可能性が高い場合（通常はそうである）に、特に意味を持つことがある。二つ以上の変数の相互作用に依存する単一の障害は、ランダムテストで検出される可能性が高い。ランダムテスト集合が、すべての\(t\)-way組合せのうち高い割合を網羅することがあるからである。しかし、複数の障害を検出する確率は\(c^m\)に従って急速に低下する。ここで、\(c =\) 網羅率（パーセント）、\(m =\) 独立した障害の数である。

contents.html: 8 ASSERTION-BASED TEST ORACLES
contents.html_ja: 8 アサーションに基づくテストオラクル

contents.html: Many programming languages include an assert feature that allows the programmer to specify properties that are assumed true at a particular point in the program. For example, a function that includes a division in which a particular parameter \(\mathrm{x}\) will be used as a divisor may require that this parameter may never be zero. This function may include the C statement assert(x != 0); as the first statement executed. Note that the assertion is not the same as an input validity check that issues an error message if input is not acceptable. The assertion gives conditions that must hold for the function to operate properly, in this case a non-zero divisor. It is the responsibility of the programmer to ensure that a zero divisor is never passed to the function. The distinction between assertions and input validation code is that assertions are intended to catch programming mistakes, while input validation detects errors in user or file/database input.
contents.html_ja: 多くのプログラミング言語にはassert機能があり、プログラマーはプログラム内の特定の時点で真と仮定される性質を指定できる。たとえば、特定のパラメーター\(\mathrm{x}\)を除数として使う除算を含む関数では、このパラメーターが決してゼロにならないことが要求される場合がある。この関数には、最初に実行される文としてCの文assert(x != 0);を含めることができる。このアサーションは、入力が許容できない場合にエラーメッセージを出す入力妥当性検査と同じではない点に注意されたい。アサーションは、関数が正しく動作するために成り立たなければならない条件、この場合はゼロでない除数を示す。ゼロの除数が決して関数に渡されないようにするのはプログラマーの責任である。アサーションと入力検証コードの違いは、アサーションがプログラミング上の誤りを捕捉するためのものであるのに対し、入力検証はユーザー入力またはファイル/データベース入力の誤りを検出する点にある。

contents.html: Many programming languages include an assert feature that allows the programmer to specify properties that are assumed true at a particular point in the program. For example, a function that includes a division in which a particular parameter x will be used as a divisor may require that this parameter may never be zero. This function may include the C statement assert(x != 0); as the first statement executed. Note that the assertion is not the same as an input validity check that issues an error message if input is not acceptable. The assertion gives conditions that must hold for the function to operate properly, in this case a non-zero divisor. It is the responsibility of the programmer to ensure that a zero divisor is never passed to the function. The distinction between assertions and input validation code is that assertions are intended to catch programming mistakes, while input validation detects errors in user or file/database input.
contents.html_ja: 多くのプログラミング言語は、プログラム中の特定の箇所で真であると仮定される性質をプログラマが指定できるアサート機能を備えている。たとえば、特定のパラメータ x を除数とする除算を含む関数では、このパラメータが決してゼロにならないことを要求する場合がある。この関数は、最初に実行される文として C の文 assert(x != 0); を含むことができる。なお、アサーションは、入力が受け入れられない場合にエラーメッセージを出す入力妥当性チェックとは異なる。アサーションは、関数が正しく動作するために満たされなければならない条件、この場合はゼロでない除数を示す。ゼロの除数が決して関数に渡されないようにするのはプログラマの責任である。アサーションと入力検証コードの違いは、アサーションがプログラミングの誤りを捕捉することを目的とするのに対し、入力検証は利用者やファイル/データベースからの入力の誤りを検出する点にある。

contents.html: With a sufficient number of assertions derived from a specification, the program can have a self-checking property [27, 60, 47]. The assertions can serve as a sort of embedded proof of important properties, such that if the assertions hold for all executions of the program, then the properties encoded in the assertions are guaranteed to hold. Then, if the assertions form a chain of logic that implies a formal statement of program properties, the program’s correctness with respect to these properties can be proven. We can take advantage of this scheme in combinatorial testing by demonstrating that the assertions hold for all t-way combinations of inputs. While this is not the same as a correctness proof, it is an effective way of integrating formal methods for correctness with program testing, and an extensive body of research has developed this idea for practical use (for a survey, see [4]). Some modern programming languages, such as Eiffel [52], include extensive support for including assertions that encode program properties, and tools such as the Java Modeling Language [42] have been designed to integrate assertions with testing. In many cases, using assertions to self-check important properties makes it practical to run thousands of tests in a fully automated fashion, so high-strength interactions of 4-way and above can be done in reasonable time.
contents.html_ja: 仕様から導出した十分な数のアサーションがあれば、プログラムに自己検査の性質を持たせることができる [27, 60, 47]。アサーションは、重要な性質の一種の組込み証明として機能しうる。すなわち、プログラムのすべての実行でアサーションが成り立つならば、アサーションに符号化された性質が成り立つことが保証される。さらに、アサーションがプログラムの性質の形式的な記述を含意する論理の連鎖を形成していれば、それらの性質に関するプログラムの正しさを証明できる。組合せテストでは、入力のすべての t 項組合せについてアサーションが成り立つことを示すことで、この仕組みを活用できる。これは正しさの証明と同じではないが、正しさのための形式手法をプログラムテストと統合する効果的な方法であり、この考え方を実用化するための研究が数多く行われてきた（概観については [4] を参照）。Eiffel [52] のような一部の現代的なプログラミング言語は、プログラムの性質を符号化するアサーションを組み込むための充実した機能を備えており、Java Modeling Language [42] のようなツールは、アサーションをテストと統合するように設計されている。多くの場合、アサーションを用いて重要な性質を自己検査することにより、数千のテストを完全に自動化して実行することが現実的になるため、4項以上の高強度の相互作用も妥当な時間で扱える。

contents.html: 8.1 Basic Assertions for Testing
contents.html_ja: 8.1 テストのための基本アサーション

contents.html: With self-checking through assertions, thousands of tests can often be run at very low cost, allowing high-strength interaction coverage.
contents.html_ja: アサーションによる自己検査を用いれば、数千のテストを非常に低いコストで実行できることが多く、高強度の相互作用カバレッジが可能になる。

contents.html: To clarify this somewhat abstract discussion, we will analyze requirements for a small function that handles withdrawal processing for an automated teller machine (ATM). Graphical user interface code for the ATM will not be displayed, as this would vary considerably for different systems. The decision not to include GUI code in this example also illustrates a practical limitation of this type of testing: there are many potential sources of error in a software project, and testing may not deal with all of them at the same time. The GUI code may be analyzed separately, or a more complex verification with assertions may specify properties of the GUI calls, but in the end some human involvement is needed to ensure that the screen information is properly displayed. However, we can do very thorough testing of the most critical aspects of the withdrawal module.

contents.html: How should these requirements be translated into assertions and used in testing? contents.html: However, we must also consider overdraft protection and withdrawal limits, so the assertion above is not adequate. Collecting conditions, we can develop assertions for each of the eight possible settings of minflag, odflag, and limflag. If there is a minimum balance requirement, no overdraft protection, and a withdrawal limit below the default, what is the relationship between balance and the other parameters?
minflag && !odflag && limflag => balance >= min – oddefault && amt <= limit
This relation must hold after the withdrawal, so to develop an assertion that must hold immediately before the withdrawal, substitute (balance – amt) for balance in the expression above:
balance0 – amt >= min – oddefault && amt <= limit

Assertions such as this would be placed immediately before the balance is modified, not at the beginning of the code for the withdrawal function. Code prior to the subtraction from balance should have ensured that properties encoded by assertions hold immediately before the subtraction, thus any violation of the assertions indicates an error in the code (or possibly in the assertions!) that must be investigated. This is illustrated in Figure 26, where “wdl_init.c” and “wdl_final.c” are files containing assertions such as developed above.

Including the card number, there are 11 parameters for this module. We need to partition the inputs to determine what values to use in generating a covering array. contents.html: 8.2 Stronger Assertion-based Testing
contents.html_ja: 8.2 より強力なアサーションベースのテスト

contents.html: While the method described in the previous section can be very effective in testing, notice that it will be inadequate for many problems, because basic assertion functions such as in C language library do not support important logic operators such as \(\forall\) (for all) and \(\exists\) (for some). Thus expressing simple properties such as \(S\) is sorted in ascending order \(= \forall i : 0 \le i < n-1 : S[i] \le S[i+1]\) cannot be done without a good deal of additional coding. While it would be possible to add code to handle these problems in assertions, a better solution is to use an assertion language that is designed for the purpose and contains all the necessary features.
contents.html_ja: 前節で説明した方法はテストに非常に有効となり得るが、多くの問題には不十分であることに注意されたい。C言語ライブラリにあるような基本的なアサーション関数は、\(\forall\)（すべての）や\(\exists\)（ある）のような重要な論理演算子をサポートしないためである。そのため、\(S\) は昇順に整列されている \(= \forall i : 0 \le i < n-1 : S[i] \le S[i+1]\) のような単純な性質であっても、相当量の追加コーディングなしには表現できない。アサーション内でこうした問題を処理するコードを追加することも可能ではあるが、この目的のために設計され、必要な機能をすべて備えたアサーション言語を使う方がよい。

contents.html: Tools such as Anna [44] for Ada, the Java Modeling language (JML) [42] and iContract [28] for Java, and APP [57] or Nana [46] for C, can be used to introduce complex assertions, effectively embedding a formal specification within the code. The embedded assertions serve as an executable form of the specification, thus providing an oracle for the testing phase. With embedded assertions, exercising the application with all \(t\)-way combinations can provide reasonable assurance that the code works correctly across a very wide range of inputs. This approach has been used successfully for testing smart cards, with embedded JML assertions acting as an oracle for combinatorial tests [25]. Results showed that 80% - 90% of errors could be found in this way.
contents.html_ja: Ada用のAnna [44]、Java用のJava Modeling language（JML）[42]およびiContract [28]、C用のAPP [57]またはNana [46]などのツールを使うと、複雑なアサーションを導入でき、実質的に形式仕様をコード内に埋め込める。埋め込まれたアサーションは仕様の実行可能な形式として働き、テスト段階のオラクルとなる。埋め込みアサーションがあれば、すべての\(t\)-way組合せでアプリケーションを実行することにより、非常に幅広い入力に対してコードが正しく動作するという妥当な保証が得られる。この方法はスマートカードのテストに用いられて成功しており、埋め込まれたJMLアサーションが組合せテストのオラクルとして機能した[25]。結果は、この方法でエラーの80%〜90%を発見できることを示した。

contents.html: 8.3 Cost and Practical Considerations
contents.html_ja: 8.3 コストと実務上の考慮事項

contents.html: Assertions may be a cost-effective approach to test automation because they can be a simple extension of coding. In general, use of assertions is correlated with reduced error rates [41], but a very wide range of effectiveness results from variations in usage. In many applications, assertions are used in a very basic way, such as ensuring that null pointers are not passed to a function that will use them, or that parameters that may be used as divisors are non-zero.
contents.html_ja: アサーションはコーディングの単純な拡張になり得るため、テスト自動化の費用対効果の高い手法となり得る。一般に、アサーションの使用はエラー率の低下と相関する[41]が、使い方の違いによって有効性は非常に大きく異なる。多くのアプリケーションでは、アサーションは、ヌルポインターを使用する関数にそれを渡さないことや、除数として使われる可能性のあるパラメーターがゼロでないことを確認するといった、ごく基本的な方法で使われている。

contents.html: More complex assertions can provide stronger assurance, but there are limits to their effectiveness. For example, invariants (properties that are expected to hold throughout a computation) cannot be assured without placing an assertion for every line of code. Since assertions must be executed to show the presence or absence of a property at some point, errors that prevent the assertion from being reached may not be detected. As an example, consider the code in Figure 26. If a coding error in the first few lines of the function prevents execution the code at of lines 15 and 17, the assertions will not be executed and it may be assumed that the test was passed. In this case, an ERROR return for the particular test case might trigger an investigation that would identify the faulty code, but this may not happen with other applications.
contents.html_ja: より複雑なアサーションはより強い保証を与えられるが、その有効性には限界がある。例えば、不変条件（計算全体を通じて成立すると期待される性質）は、コードのすべての行にアサーションを置かない限り保証できない。アサーションは、ある時点での性質の有無を示すために実行されなければならないため、アサーションに到達するのを妨げる誤りは検出されない場合がある。例として、図26のコードを考える。関数の最初の数行にコーディング誤りがあり、15行目と17行目のコードが実行されない場合、アサーションは実行されず、テストに合格したと見なされる可能性がある。この場合、特定のテストケースでERRORが返ることで、欠陥のあるコードを特定する調査が始まるかもしれないが、他のアプリケーションではそうならないことがある。

contents.html: 8.4 Chapter Summary
contents.html_ja: 8.4 本章の要約

contents.html: Assertions are one of the easiest to use and most effective approaches to dealing with the oracle problem. Properties ranging from simple parameter checks to effectively embedded proofs can be encoded in assertions, but special language support is needed for the stronger forms of assurance. This support may be provided as language preprocessors, as in the case of Anna [44] and others. Placement within code is particularly important to assertion effectiveness [60, 61], but if sufficiently strong assertions are embedded, the code becomes self-checking for important properties. With self-checking code, thousands of tests can be run at low cost in most cases, greatly improving the chances that faults will be detected.
contents.html_ja: アサーションは、オラクル問題に対処する方法のうち、最も使いやすく最も効果的なものの一つである。単純なパラメータ検査から、実質的に埋め込まれた証明に至るまで、さまざまな性質をアサーションとして記述できるが、より強い形の保証には専用の言語サポートが必要である。このサポートは、Anna [44]などの場合のように、言語プリプロセッサとして提供されることがある。コード内での配置はアサーションの有効性にとって特に重要である[60, 61]が、十分に強いアサーションを埋め込めば、コードは重要な性質について自己検査するようになる。自己検査コードがあれば、ほとんどの場合、数千件のテストを低コストで実行でき、障害が検出される可能性が大幅に高まる。

contents.html: 9 MODEL-BASED TEST ORACLES
contents.html_ja: 9 モデルに基づくテストオラクル

contents.html: One of the most effective ways to produce test oracles is to use a model of the system under test, and generate complete tests, including both input data and expected results, directly from the model. The model in this case is exactly what the name implies: it incorporates the most important aspects of the system, but not every detail such as the location of an amount on a screen (if it did include all details, it would be equivalent to the system itself). This chapter provides a step-by-step introduction to model-based automated generation of tests that provide combinatorial coverage. Procedures introduced in this tutorial will produce a set of complete tests, i.e., input values with the expected output for each set of inputs.
contents.html_ja: テストオラクルを作成する最も効果的な方法の一つは、テスト対象システムのモデルを使い、入力データと期待結果の両方を含む完全なテストをモデルから直接生成することである。ここでいうモデルは、まさにその名が示すとおりのものである。すなわち、システムの最も重要な側面を取り込むが、画面上の金額の位置のような細部までは含まない（すべての細部を含むなら、システムそのものと等価になる）。本章では、組合せ網羅を与えるテストのモデルベース自動生成を段階的に紹介する。このチュートリアルで紹介する手順により、完全なテストの集合、すなわち入力値と各入力セットに対する期待出力が生成される。

contents.html: Also needed is a formal or semi-formal specification of the system or subsystem under test (SUT). This can be in the form of a formal logic specification, but state transition tables, decision tables, pseudo-code, or structured natural language can also be used, as long as the rules are unambiguous. The specification will be converted to SMV code, which provides a precise, machine-processable set of rules that can be used to generate tests.

contents.html: Using ACTS, construct a set of tests that will cover all t-way combinations of parameter values. The covering array specifies test data, where each row of the array can be regarded as a set of parameter values for an individual test (see Chapter 4).

contents.html: 2. Determine what output should be produced by the SUT for each set of input parameter values. The test data output from ACTS will be incorporated into SMV specifications that can be processed by the NuSMV model checker for this step. The example in Section 9.2.1 illustrates a simple conversion of rules in the form “if condition then action” into the syntax used by the model checker. The model checker will instantiate the specification with parameter values from the covering array once for each test in the covering array. The resulting specification is evaluated against a claim that negates each specified result Rj using a model checker, so that the model checker evaluates claims in the following form: Ci => ~Rj, where Ci is a set of parameter values in one row of the covering array in the form p1 = vi1 & p2 = vi2 & ... & pn = vin, and Rj is one of the possible results. The output of this step is a set of counterexamples that show how the SUT can reach the claimed result Rj from a given set of inputs.

For example, in some cases we can run a model checker in simulation mode, producing expected results directly rather than through a counterexample.

contents.html: The completed tests can be used to validate correct operation of the system for interaction strengths up to some pre-determined level \(t\). Depending on the system type and level of effort, we may want to use pairwise (\(t=2\)) or higher strength, up to \(t=6\) way interactions. We do not claim this guarantees correctness of the system, as there may be failures triggered only by interaction strengths greater than \(t\). In addition, some of the parameters are likely to have a large number of possible values, requiring that they be abstracted into equivalence classes. If the abstraction does not faithfully represent the range of values for a parameter, some flaws may not be detected by equivalence classes used.

contents.html: Separate documentation on SMV should be consulted to fully understand the syntax used, but specifications of the form “AG ((predicate 1) -> AX (predicate 2))” indicate essentially that for all paths (the “A” in “AG”) for all states globally (the “G”), if predicate 1 holds then ( “->”) for all paths, in the next state (the “X” in “AX”) predicate 2 will hold. In the next section we will see how this specification can be used to produce complete tests, with test data input and the expected output for each set of input data.
contents.html_ja: SMVの構文を完全に理解するには別途資料を参照すべきであるが、「AG ((predicate 1) -> AX (predicate 2))」形式の仕様は、基本的に、すべての経路（「AG」の「A」）について、すべての状態で（「AG」の「G」）、述語1が成立すれば（「->」）、次状態（「AX」の「X」）ですべての経路において述語2が成立することを示す。次節では、この仕様を使って、入力テストデータと各入力セットに対する期待出力を含む完全なテストを作成する方法を説明する。

contents.html: Model checkers can be used to perform a variety of valuable functions, because they make it possible to evaluate whether certain properties are true of the system model. Conceptually, the model checker can be viewed as exploring all states of a system model to determine if a property claimed in a SPEC statement is true. If the statement can be proved true for the given model, the model checker reports this fact. What makes a model checker particularly valuable for many applications, though, is that if the statement is false, the model checker not only reports this, but also provides a “counterexample” showing how the claim in the SPEC statement can be shown false. The counterexample will include input data values and a trace of system states that lead to a result contrary to the SPEC claim (Figure 28). In the process described in this section, the input data values will be the covering array generated by ACTS.
contents.html_ja: モデルチェッカーは、システムモデル上で特定の性質が成立するかどうかを評価できるため、さまざまな有用な機能を実行できる。概念的には、モデルチェッカーはシステムモデルの全状態を調べ、SPEC文で主張された性質が真かどうかを判定するものと考えられる。所与のモデルで文が真と証明できれば、その事実を報告する。しかし、多くの用途でモデルチェッカーが特に有用なのは、文が偽の場合、その事実を報告するだけでなく、SPEC文の主張が偽となる方法を示す「反例」も提示する点である。反例には、入力データ値と、SPECの主張に反する結果に至るシステム状態のトレースが含まれる（図28）。本節で説明する手順では、入力データ値にACTSが生成したカバリングアレイを用いる。

contents.html: For advanced uses in test generation, this counterexample generation capability is very useful for proving properties such as liveness (absence of deadlock) that are difficult to ensure through testing. In this tutorial, however, we will simply use the model checker to determine whether a particular input data set makes a SPEC claim true or false. That is, we will enter claims that particular results can be reached for a given set of input data values, and the model checker will tell us if the claim is true or false. This gives us the ability to match every set of input test data with the result that the system should produce for that input data.
contents.html_ja: テスト生成における高度な用途では、この反例生成機能は、テストでは保証しにくい活性（デッドロックがないこと）などの性質を証明するうえで非常に有用である。ただしこのチュートリアルでは、特定の入力データセットがSPECの主張を真にするか偽にするかを判定するためだけにモデルチェッカーを使う。すなわち、与えられた入力データ値の集合に対して特定の結果に到達できるという主張を入力し、その主張が真か偽かをモデルチェッカーに判定させる。これにより、入力テストデータのすべての集合を、その入力データに対してシステムが生成すべき結果と対応付けられる。

contents.html: The model checker thus automates the work that normally must be done by a human tester – determining what the correct output should be for each set of input data. In some cases, we may have a “reference implementation”, that is, an implementation of the functions that we are testing that is assumed to be correct. This happens, for example, in conformance testing for protocols, where many vendors implement their own software for the protocol and submit it to a test lab for comparison with an existing implementation of the protocol. In this case the reference implementation could be used for determining the expected output, instead of the model checker. Of course before this can happen the reference implementation itself must be thoroughly tested before it can be used as the gold standard for testing other products, so the method we describe here may be needed to produce tests for the original reference implementation.
contents.html_ja: このようにモデルチェッカーは、通常は人間のテスターが行わなければならない作業、すなわち各入力データセットに対する正しい出力が何であるかを決める作業を自動化する。場合によっては「参照実装」、すなわちテスト対象の機能の実装のうち正しいと仮定されるものが存在する。これはたとえばプロトコルの適合性試験で生じる。そこでは多くのベンダーがプロトコルの独自ソフトウェアを実装し、プロトコルの既存実装と比較するために試験機関へ提出する。この場合、モデルチェッカーの代わりに参照実装を使って期待出力を決定できる。もちろんその前に、他の製品をテストするためのゴールドスタンダードとして使えるよう、参照実装そのものを徹底的にテストしなければならない。したがって、元の参照実装のテストを生成するために、ここで述べる方法が必要になる場合がある。

contents.html: Checking the properties in the SPEC statements shows that they match the access control rules as implemented in the FSM, as expected. In other words, the claims we made about the state machine in the SPEC clauses can be proven. This step is used to check that the SPEC claims are valid for the model defined previously. If NuSMV is unable to prove one of the SPECs, then either the spec or the model is incorrect. This problem must be resolved before continuing with the test generation process. Once the model is correct and SPEC claims have been shown valid for the model, counterexamples can be produced that will be turned into test cases, by which we mean a set of test inputs with the expected result for these inputs. In other words, ACTS is used to generate tests, then the model checker determines expected results for each test.

This means that any legitimate value for that parameter can be used and the full set of configurations will still cover all \(\mathrm{t}\)-way combinations. contents.html: 9.3 Cost and Practical Considerations
contents.html_ja: 9.3 コストと実務上の考慮事項

contents.html: Model based test generation trades up-front analysis and specification time against the cost of greater human interaction for analyzing test results. The model or formal specification may be costly to produce, but once it is available, large numbers of tests can be generated, executed, and analyzed without human intervention. This can be an enormous cost savings, since testing usually requires 50% or more of the software development budget. For example, suppose a $100,000 development project expects to spend $50,000 on testing, because of the staff time required to code and run tests, and analyze results. If a formal model can be created for $20,000, complete tests generated and analyzed automatically, with another $10,000 for a smaller number of human-involved tests and analysis, then the project will save 20%. One tradeoff for this savings is the requirement for staff with skills in formal methods, but in some cases this approach may be practical and highly cost-effective.
contents.html_ja: モデルベースのテスト生成では、事前の分析と仕様化に時間をかける代わりに、テスト結果の分析に人手を多く要するコストを抑える。モデルまたは形式仕様の作成には費用がかかる場合があるが、いったん用意できれば、大量のテストを人手を介さずに生成、実行、分析できる。テストには通常、ソフトウェア開発予算の50%以上が必要となるため、これは大幅なコスト削減になり得る。例えば、テストのコーディングと実行、結果の分析に要する要員の工数のために、開発費10万ドルのプロジェクトでテストに5万ドルを費やすと見込まれるとする。形式モデルを2万ドルで作成でき、完全なテストが自動的に生成・分析され、人手が関与する少数のテストと分析にさらに1万ドルかかるなら、プロジェクトは20%を節約できる。この節約に伴うトレードオフの1つは、形式手法の技能を持つ要員が必要になることだが、場合によってはこの手法は実用的であり、費用対効果が非常に高い。

contents.html: 9.4 Chapter Summary
contents.html_ja: 9.4 本章のまとめ

contents.html: The oracle problem must be solved for any test methodology, and it is particularly important for thorough testing that produces a large number of test cases. One approach to determining expected results for each test input is to use a model of the system that can be simulated or analyzed to compute output for each input.
contents.html_ja: オラクル問題はどのようなテスト手法でも解決しなければならず、多数のテストケースを生成する徹底的なテストでは特に重要である。各テスト入力に対する期待結果を決定する方法の一つは、シミュレーションまたは解析によって各入力に対する出力を計算できるシステムのモデルを使うことである。

contents.html: Model checkers can be used to solve the oracle problem because whenever a specified property for a model does not hold, the model checker generates a counter-example. The counter-example can be post-processed into a complete working test harness that executes all tests from the covering array and checks results.
contents.html_ja: モデルチェッカーはオラクル問題の解決に使える。モデルに対して指定された性質が成り立たない場合は必ず、モデルチェッカーが反例を生成するためである。この反例を後処理することで、被覆配列のすべてのテストを実行し結果を検査する、完全に動作するテストハーネスにできる。

contents.html: Several approaches are possible for integrating combinatorial testing with model checkers, but some present practical problems. The method reported in this chapter can be used to generate full combinatorial test suites, with expected results for each test, in a cost effective way.
contents.html_ja: 組合せテストをモデルチェッカーと統合する方法はいくつか考えられるが、実務上の問題を伴うものもある。本章で報告した方法を使えば、各テストの期待結果を伴う完全な組合せテストスイートを、費用対効果の高い方法で生成できる。

contents.html: 10 FAULT LOCALIZATION
contents.html_ja: 10 障害箇所の特定

contents.html: Developing dependable software requires preventing as many bugs as possible and detecting, then repairing, those that remain. Testing can identify flaws in software, but after a failed test is discovered, it is necessary to determine what caused the failure. In most cases this may be accomplished for combinatorial testing in the same way as other test methodologies, using a debugger or in-circuit emulator. But one goal of combinatorial testing is to identify the particular t-way combination that triggered a failure. The problem of fault localization, identifying such combination(s), is an area of active research, but some basic approaches can be identified. The discussion in this chapter assumes systems are deterministic, such that a particular input always generates the same output.
contents.html_ja: 信頼できるソフトウェアを開発するには、できるだけ多くのバグを防ぎ、残ったバグを検出して修正する必要がある。テストによってソフトウェアの欠陥を特定できるが、失敗したテストが見つかった後は、何が障害の原因となったかを突き止める必要がある。多くの場合、組合せテストでもこれは他のテスト手法と同じように、デバッガやインサーキットエミュレータを用いて行える。しかし、組合せテストの目的の一つは、障害を引き起こした特定の t 項組合せを特定することである。そのような組合せを特定する障害箇所の特定の問題は活発に研究されている分野であるが、いくつかの基本的な手法を挙げることができる。本章の議論では、システムは決定的であり、特定の入力が常に同じ出力を生成すると仮定する。

contents.html: At first glance, fault localization may not appear to be a difficult problem, and in many cases it will not be, but we want to automate the process as much as possible. To understand the size of the problem, consider a module that has 20 input parameters. A set of 3-way covering tests passes 100%, but several tests derived from a 4-way covering array result in failure. (Therefore, at least four parameter values are involved in triggering the failure. It is possible that a 5-way or higher combination caused the failure, since any set of t-way tests also includes (t+1)-way and higher strength combinations as well.) A test with 20 input parameters has C(20, 4) = 4,845 4-way combinations, yet presumably only one (or just a few) of these triggered the failure. To determine the combination at fault, a variety of strategies can be used.
contents.html_ja: 一見すると、障害箇所の特定は難しい問題には見えないかもしれず、実際多くの場合は難しくないが、このプロセスはできるだけ自動化したい。問題の規模を理解するために、20個の入力パラメータを持つモジュールを考える。3項カバリングテストのセットはすべて合格するが、4項カバリング配列から導出したいくつかのテストが失敗する（したがって、障害の発生には少なくとも4つのパラメータ値が関与している。t 項テストのセットは (t+1) 項以上の強度の組合せも含むため、5項以上の組合せが障害を引き起こした可能性もある）。20個の入力パラメータを持つテストには C(20, 4) = 4,845 個の4項組合せがあるが、そのうち障害を引き起こしたのはおそらく1つ（またはごく少数）だけである。障害の原因となった組合せを特定するには、さまざまな戦略を用いることができる。

contents.html: 10.1 Set-theoretic Analysis
contents.html_ja: 10.1 集合論的分析

contents.html: The analysis presented here applies to a deterministic system, in which a particular set of input values always results in the same processing and outputs. Let P = {combinations in passing tests} and F = {combinations in failing tests} and C = {fault-triggering combinations}. Then F \ P , combinations in failing tests that are not in any passing tests, must contain the fault-triggering combinations C because if any of those in C were in P, then the test would have failed. So in most cases, C ⊆ F \ P , as shown in Figure 30.
contents.html_ja: ここで示す分析は、特定の入力値の組が常に同じ処理と出力をもたらす決定的なシステムに適用される。P = {合格したテスト中の組合せ}、F = {失敗したテスト中の組合せ}、C = {障害を引き起こす組合せ} とする。このとき、F \ P 、すなわち失敗したテストに含まれ、どの合格したテストにも含まれない組合せは、障害を引き起こす組合せ C を含んでいなければならない。C の組合せのいずれかが P に含まれていたとすれば、そのテストは失敗していたはずだからである。したがって、ほとんどの場合、図30に示すように C ⊆ F \ P となる。

contents.html: Elimination: For a deterministic system, F \ P must contain the fault-triggering combinations C because if any of those in C were in P, then the test would have failed.

contents.html: • Interaction level lower bound: If all \(t\)-way tests pass, then a \(t\)-way or lower strength combination did not cause the failure. The failure must have been caused by a \((t+k)\)-way combination, for some \(k > t\). Note that the converse is not necessarily true: if some \(t\)-way test fails, we cannot conclude that a \(t\)-way test caused the failure, because any \(t\)-way test set contains some \(k\)-way combinations, for \(k > t\).
contents.html_ja: • 相互作用レベルの下限：すべての\(t\)-wayテストが合格した場合、\(t\)-way以下の強度の組合せが失敗を引き起こしたのではない。失敗は、\((t+k)\)-way組合せ（ある\(k > t\)について）が引き起こしたはずである。ただし逆は必ずしも成り立たない点に注意する。ある\(t\)-wayテストが失敗しても、\(t\)-wayテストが失敗を引き起こしたと結論することはできない。任意の\(t\)-wayテスト集合には、\(k\)-way組合せ（\(k > t\)）も含まれるためである。

contents.html: • Interaction continuity: Now consider \(Ct\). Because \(t\)-way tests cover all combinations of \(t\)-way or lower strength (e.g., 4-way tests also cover all 3-way combinations), a combination that triggered the failure in \(Ft\) must also occur in \(F(t+1)\), \(F(t+2)\), etc. Therefore we can further reduce the potential failure-triggering combinations by computing \(Ft \cap F(t+1) \cap \ldots \cap F(t+k)\) for whatever interaction strength \(k\) we have tests available.

contents.html: When source code is available, the best way to identify the cause of a failure is with conventional debugging techniques, since the error must be fixed in code anyway. With pure black-box testing and no access to source code, the heuristics discussed in this chapter may help to narrow down possible causes. Usually there will be many combinations identified as possible causes, so substantial additional testing may be needed to determine the exact cause.

Orthogonal Arrays

Many software testing problems can be solved with an orthogonal array, a structure that has been used for combinatorial testing in fields other than software for decades. An orthogonal array, OAλ (N;t,k,v) is an N x k array. In every N x t subarray, each t-tuple occurs exactly λ times. We refer to t as the strength of the coverage of interactions, k as the number of parameters or components (degree), and v as the number of possible values for each parameter or component (order).

Example. Suppose we have a system with three on-off switches, controlled by an embedded processor. The following table tests all pairs of switch settings exactly once each. Thus \(t = 2\), \(\lambda = 1\), \(v = 2\). Note that there are \(v^t = 2^2\) possible combinations of values for each pair: 00, 01, 10, 11. There are \(\mathrm{C}(3,2) = 3\) ways to select switch pairs: (1,2), (1,3), and (2,3), and each test covers three pairs, so the four tests cover a total of 12 combinations which implies that each combination is covered exactly once. As one might suspect, it can be very challenging to fit all combinations to be covered into a set of tests exactly the same number of times.

contents.html: Covering Arrays
contents.html_ja: カバリングアレイ

contents.html: An alternative to an orthogonal array is a set called a covering array, which includes all \(t\)-way combinations of parameter values, for the desired strength \(t\). A covering array, \(\mathit{CA}_{\lambda}(N;t,k,v)\), is an \(N \times k\) array. In every \(N \times t\) subarray, each \(t\)-tuple occurs at least \(\lambda\) times. Note this distinction between covering arrays and orthogonal arrays discussed in the previous section. The covering array relaxes the restriction that each combination is covered exactly the same number of times. Thus covering arrays may result in some test duplication, but they offer the advantage that they can be computed for much larger problems than is possible for orthogonal arrays. Software described elsewhere in this book can efficiently generate covering arrays up to strength \(t = 6\), for a large number of variables.
contents.html_ja: 直交配列に代わるものとして、被覆配列と呼ばれる集合がある。被覆配列は、求める強度\(t\)について、パラメータ値の\(t\)-way組合せをすべて含む。被覆配列\(\mathit{CA}_{\lambda}(N;t,k,v)\)は\(N \times k\)の配列である。どの\(N \times t\)部分配列においても、各\(t\)タプルは少なくとも\(\lambda\)回出現する。前節で述べた直交配列と被覆配列とのこの違いに注意されたい。被覆配列は、各組合せがちょうど同じ回数だけ網羅されるという制約を緩めている。そのため、被覆配列ではテストにいくらか重複が生じることがあるが、直交配列で可能な規模よりはるかに大きな問題に対して計算できるという利点がある。本書の別の箇所で説明するソフトウェアは、多数の変数に対して、強度\(t = 6\)までの被覆配列を効率よく生成できる。

contents.html: The problems discussed in this publication deal only with the case when \(\lambda = 1\), (i.e. that every \(t\)-tuple must be covered at least once). In software testing, each row of the covering array represents a test, with one column for each parameter that is varied in testing. Collectively, the rows of the array include every \(t\)-way combination of parameter values at least once. For example, Figure 1 shows a covering array that includes all 3-way combinations of binary values for 10 parameters. Each column gives the values for a particular parameter. It can be seen that any three columns in any order contain all eight possible combinations of the parameter values. Collectively, this set of tests will exercise all 3-way combinations of input values in only 13 tests, as compared with 1,024 for exhaustive coverage.

contents.html: The challenge in computing covering arrays is to find the smallest possible array that covers all configurations of t variables. If every new test generated covered all previously uncovered combinations, then the number of tests needed would be
\(\frac{v^t \binom{n}{t}}{\binom{n}{t}} = v^t\)

Since this is not generally possible, the covering array will be significantly larger than \(v^t\), but still a reasonable number for testing. It can be shown that the number of tests in a t-way covering array will be proportional to
\(v^t \log n\) (2)
for n variables with v values each.

It’s worth considering the components of this expression to gain a better understanding of what will be required to do combinatorial testing. Although the number of tests required for high-strength combinatorial testing can be very large, with advanced software and cluster processors it is not out of reach.

Despite the possibly discouraging numbers in the table above, there is some good news. Note that formula (2) grows only logarithmically with the number of variables, n. This is fortunate for software testing. Early applications of combinatorial methods were typically involved with small numbers of variables, such as a few different types of crops or fertilizers, but for software testing, we must deal with tens, or in some cases hundreds of variables.
Regular Expressions

Regular expressions are formal descriptions of strings of symbols, which may represent text, events, characters, or other objects. They are developed within automata theory and formal languages, where it is shown that there are direct mappings between expressions and automata to process them, and are encountered in many areas within computer science. In combinatorial testing they may be encountered in sequence covering or in processing test input or output. Implementations vary, but standard syntax is explained below.
Expression Operators
Basic elements of regular expressions include:
| — “or” alternation. Ex: ab|ac matches “ab” or “ac”
? — 0 or 1 of the preceding element. Ex: ab?c matches “ac” or “abc”
* — 0 or more of the preceding element. Ex: ab* matches “a”, “ab”, “abb”, “abbb” etc.
+ — 1 or more of the preceding element. Ex: ab+ matches “ab”, “abb”, “abbb” etc.
() — grouping. Ex: (abc|abcd) matches “abc” or “abcd”
. — matches any single character. Ex: a.c matches “abc”, “axc”, “a@c” etc.

[ ] — matches any single character within brackets. Ex: [abc] matches “a” or “b” or “c”. A range may also be specified. Ex: [a-z] matches any single lower case character. (This option depends on the character set supported.)
[^ ] — matches any single character that is not contained in the brackets. Ex: [^ab] matches any character except “a” or “b”
^ — matches start position, i.e., before the first character
$ — matches end position, i.e., after the last character
Combining Operators
The operators above can be combined with symbols to create arbitrarily complex expressions. Examples include:
.*a.*b.*c.* — “a” followed by “b” followed by “c” with zero or more symbols prior to “a”, following “c”, or interspersed with the three symbols
a|b* — null or “a” or zero or more occurrences of “b”
a+ — equivalent to aa*

Many regular expression utilities such as egrep support a broader range of operators and features. Readers should consult documentation for grep, egrep, or other regular expression processors for detailed coverage of the options available on particular tools.
Appendix B - EMPIRICAL DATA ON SOFTWARE FAILURES
contents.html_ja: 付録B - ソフトウェア障害に関する実証データ

contents.html: One of the most important questions in software testing is "how much is enough"? For combinatorial testing, this question includes determining the appropriate level of interaction that should be tested. That is, if some failure is triggered only by an unusual combination of more than two values, how many testing combinations are enough to detect all errors? What degree of interaction occurs in real system failures? This section summarizes what is known about these questions based on research by NIST and others [4, 7, 34, 35, 36, 65].
contents.html_ja: ソフトウェアテストにおける最も重要な問いの1つは、「どれだけやれば十分か」である。組合せテストでは、この問いに、テストすべき相互作用の適切な水準を決めることが含まれる。つまり、ある失敗が2つを超える値の珍しい組合せによってのみ引き起こされるとしたら、すべてのエラーを検出するにはいくつの組合せをテストすれば十分なのか。実際のシステムの失敗では、どの程度の相互作用が生じているのか。本節では、NISTほかによる研究[4, 7, 34, 35, 36, 65]に基づき、これらの問いについて分かっていることをまとめる。

contents.html: Why do the failure detection curves look this way? That is, why does the error rate tail off so rapidly with more variables interacting? One possibility is that there are simply few complex interactions in branching points in software. If few branches involve 4-way, 5-way, or 6-way interactions among variables, then this degree of interaction could be rare for failures as well. The table below (Table 4 and Fig. 2) gives the number and percentage of branches in avionics code triggered by one to 19 variables. This distribution was developed by analyzing data in a report on the use of MCDC testing in avionics software [16], which contains 20,256 logic expressions in five different airborne systems in two different airplane models. The table below includes all 7,685 expressions from if and while statements; expressions from assignment (:=) statements were excluded.
contents.html_ja: 障害検出曲線がこのような形になるのはなぜか。つまり、相互作用する変数が増えるとエラー率が急速に低下するのはなぜか。考えられる理由の1つは、ソフトウェアの分岐点に複雑な相互作用がほとんどないことである。変数間の4-way、5-way、6-way相互作用を含む分岐が少なければ、この程度の相互作用が障害を引き起こすこともまれである可能性がある。下の表（表4および図2）は、航空電子機器コードにおいて1～19個の変数によって実行される分岐の数と割合を示す。この分布は、航空電子機器ソフトウェアのMCDC試験利用に関する報告書 [16] のデータを分析して作成された。同報告書には、2種類の航空機モデルに搭載された5つの異なるシステムにおける20,256個の論理式が含まれる。下の表にはif文およびwhile文に含まれる式7,685個すべてを含め、代入（:=）文の式は除外した。

contents.html: As shown in Fig. 2, most branching statement expressions are simple, with over 70% containing only a single variable. Superimposing the curve from Fig. 2 on Fig. 1, we see (Fig. 3) that most failures are triggered by more complex interactions among variables. It is interesting that the NASA distributed database failures, from development-phase software bug reports, have a distribution similar to expressions in branching statements. This distribution may be because this was development-phase rather than fielded software like all other types reported in Fig. 1. As failures are removed, the remaining failures may be harder to find because they require the interaction of more variables. Thus testing and use may push the curve down and to the right.

contents.html: Appendix C - TOOLS FOR COMBINATORIAL TESTING
contents.html_ja: 付録C - 組合せテスト用ツール

contents.html: A variety of software tools are available to assist with combinatorial testing projects. Here we summarize those available from the NIST ACTS project. The ACTS covering array generator is generally faster and produces smaller test arrays than others, based on comparisons we have done in 2009. The other tools, to the best of our knowledge, have functions that are not available elsewhere.
contents.html_ja: 組合せテストプロジェクトを支援するさまざまなソフトウェアツールが利用できる。ここではNIST ACTSプロジェクトで提供されるツールを要約する。2009年に実施した比較に基づくと、ACTS被覆配列生成器は一般に他のツールより高速で、小さいテスト配列を生成する。他のツールには、私たちの知る限り、他では利用できない機能がある。

contents.html: ACTS covering array generator – produces compact arrays that will cover 2-way through 6-way combinations. It also supports constraints that can make some values dependent on others, and mixed level covering arrays which offer different strength coverage for subsets of the parameters (e.g., 2-way coverage for one subset but 4-way for another subset of parameters). Output can be exported in a variety of formats, including human-readable, numeric, and spreadsheet. Either “don’t care” or randomized output can be specified for tests that include combinations already fully covered by previous tests.
contents.html_ja: ACTS被覆配列生成器 — 2-wayから6-wayまでの組合せを網羅するコンパクトな配列を生成する。また、一部の値を他の値に依存させる制約や、パラメーターの部分集合ごとに異なる強度の網羅率（例: ある部分集合では2-way、別の部分集合では4-way）を提供する混合レベル被覆配列もサポートする。出力は、人間可読形式、数値形式、スプレッドシート形式など、さまざまな形式でエクスポートできる。以前のテストですでに完全に網羅された組合せを含むテストについては、「ドントケア」またはランダム出力を指定できる。

contents.html: Coverage measurement tool – produces a comprehensive set of data on the combinatorial coverage of an existing set of tests, as explained in Chapter 6. Output can be generated in spreadsheet format to allow easy processing and graphing.
contents.html_ja: 網羅率測定ツール — 第6章で説明したように、既存のテスト集合の組合せ網羅率に関する包括的なデータを生成する。容易に処理およびグラフ化できるよう、スプレッドシート形式で出力できる。

contents.html: Sequence covering array generator – produces sequence covering arrays as defined in Chapter 5. It includes an option for constraints in the form of prohibited sequences.
contents.html_ja: シーケンス被覆配列生成器 — 第5章で定義したシーケンス被覆配列を生成する。禁止シーケンス形式の制約オプションを含む。

contents.html: To obtain any of these, see the ACTS web site at csrc.nist.gov/acts.

original_blocks.html: An alternative to an orthogonal array is a set called a covering array, which includes all t-way combinations of parameter values, for the desired strength t. A covering array, CAλ(N;t,k,v) , is an N x k array. In every N x t subarray, each t-tuple occurs at least λ times. Note this distinction between covering arrays and orthogonal arrays discussed in the previous section. The covering array relaxes the restriction that each combination is covered exactly the same number of times. Thus covering arrays may result in some test duplication, but they offer the advantage that they can be computed for much larger problems than is possible for orthogonal arrays. Testing all 4-way to 6-way combinations may therefore provide reasonably high assurance. As with most issues in software, however, the situation is not that simple. Efficient generation of test suites to cover all t-way combinations is a difficult mathematical problem that has been studied for nearly a century. In addition, most parameters are continuous variables which have possible values in a very large range (+/ 232 or more). These values must be discretized to a few distinct values. Most glaring of all is the problem of determining the correct result that should be expected from the system under test for each set of test inputs. Generating 1,000 test data inputs is of little help if we cannot determine what the system under test (SUT) should produce as output for each of the 1,000 tests.

For example, suppose we had an application that is intended to run on a variety of platforms comprised of five components: an operating system (Windows XP, Apple OS X, Red Hat Enterprise Linux), a browser (Internet Explorer, Firefox), protocol stack (IPv4, IPv6), a processor (Intel, AMD), and a database (MySQL, Sybase, Oracle), a total of 3⋅2⋅2⋅2⋅3 = 72 possible platforms. With only 10 tests, shown in Table 1, it is possible to test every component interacting with every other component at least once, i.e., all possible pairs of platform components are covered.

Even in the absence of knowledge about a program’s inner structure, we can apply combinatorial methods to produce precise and useful measures. In this case, we measure the state space of inputs. Suppose we have a program that accepts two inputs, x and y, with 10 values each. Then the input state space consists of the 102 = 100 pairs of x and y values, which can be pictured as a checkerboard square of 10 rows by 10 columns. With three inputs, x, y, and z, we would have a cube with 103 = 1,000 points in its input state space. Extending the example to n inputs we would have a (hard to visualize) hypercube of n dimensions with 10n points. Exhaustive testing would require inputs of all 10n combinations, but combinatorial testing could be used to reduce the size of the test set.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Combinatorial testing can help detect problems like this early in the testing life cycle. The key insight underlying t-way combinatorial testing is that not every parameter contributes to every failure and most failures are triggered by a single parameter value or interactions between a relatively small number of parameters (for more on the number of parameters interacting in failures, see Appendix B). To detect interaction failures, software developers often use “pairwise testing”, in which all possible pairs of parameter values are covered by at least one test. Its effectiveness is based on the observation that software failures often involve interactions between parameters. For example, a router may be observed to fail only for a particular protocol when packet volume exceeds a certain rate, a 2-way interaction between protocol type and packet rate. Figure 1 illustrates how such a 2-way interaction may happen in code. Note that the failure will only be triggered when both pressure < 10 and volume > 300 are true.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 組合せテストは、テストライフサイクルの早い段階で、このような問題を検出するのに役立つ。t-way組合せテストの基礎となる重要な洞察は、すべてのパラメーターがあらゆる障害に関与するわけではなく、ほとんどの障害は単一のパラメーター値、または比較的少数のパラメーター間の相互作用によって引き起こされるという点である（障害に関与するパラメーター数については付録Bを参照）。相互作用障害を検出するため、ソフトウェア開発者はしばしば「ペアワイズテスト」を用いる。これは、すべてのパラメーター値の組合せペアを少なくとも1つのテストで網羅する方法である。その有効性は、ソフトウェア障害にはパラメーター間の相互作用がしばしば関与するという観察に基づいている。例えば、ルーターが、特定のプロトコルで、パケット量が一定の速度を超えた場合にのみ故障することがある。これは、プロトコルの種類とパケット速度の2-way相互作用である。図1は、コード内でこのような2-way相互作用が起きる例を示す。pressure < 10とvolume > 300の両方が真の場合にのみ、障害が引き起こされることに注意されたい。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Pairwise testing can be highly effective and good tools are available to generate arrays with all pairs of parameter value combinations. But until recently only a handful of tools could generate combinations beyond 2-way, and most that did could require impractically long times to generate 3-way, 4-way, or 5-way arrays because the generation process is mathematically complex. Pairwise testing, i.e. 2-way combinations, has come to be accepted as the common approach to combinatorial testing because it is computationally tractable and reasonably effective.

rebuilt_blocks.html: There are basically two approaches to combinatorial testing – use combinations of configuration parameter values, or combinations of input parameter values. In the first case, we select combinations of values of configurable parameters. For example, a server might be tested by setting up all 4-way combinations of configuration parameters such as number of simultaneous connections allowed, memory, OS, database size, etc., with the same test suite run against each configuration. The tests may have been constructed using any methodology, not necessarily combinatorial coverage. The combinatorial aspect of this approach is in achieving combinatorial coverage of configuration parameter values. (Note, the term variable is often used interchangeably with parameter to refer to inputs to a function.)

rebuilt_blocks.html: Crash testing: the easiest and least expensive approach is to simply run tests against the system under test (SUT) to check whether any unusual combination of input values causes a crash or other easily detectable failure. This is essentially the same procedure used in “fuzz testing”, which sends random values against the SUT. This form of combinatorial testing could be regarded as a disciplined form of fuzz testing [59]. It should be noted that although pure random testing will generally cover a high percentage of t-way combinations, 100% coverage of combinations requires a random test set much larger than a covering array. For example, all 3-way combinations of 10 parameters with 4 values each can be covered with 151 tests. Purely random generation requires over 900 tests to provide full 3-way coverage. Embedded assertions: An increasingly popular “light-weight formal methods” technique is to embed assertions within code to ensure proper relationships between data, for example as preconditions, postconditions, or input value checks. Tools such as the Java Modeling language (JML) can be used to introduce very complex assertions, effectively embedding a formal specification within the code. The embedded assertions serve as an executable form of the specification, thus providing an oracle for the testing phase. With embedded assertions, exercising the application with all t-way combinations can provide reasonable assurance that the code works correctly across a very wide range of inputs. This approach has been used successfully for testing smart cards, with embedded JML assertions acting as an oracle for combinatorial tests [25]. Results showed that 80% - 90% of errors could be found in this way.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: クラッシュテスト: 最も簡単で費用のかからない方法は、被試験システム（SUT）に対してテストを実行し、入力値の異常な組合せがクラッシュやその他容易に検出できる障害を引き起こすか確認することである。これは基本的に「ファズテスト」で用いる手順と同じであり、SUTにランダムな値を送る。この組合せテストは、規律あるファズテストと見なせる [59]。純粋なランダムテストは一般に高い割合のt-way組合せを網羅するものの、組合せを100%網羅するには、被覆配列よりはるかに大きなランダムテスト集合が必要となる点に留意されたい。たとえば、各々4つの値を持つ10個のパラメーターの3-way組合せは、151件のテストで網羅できる。純粋なランダム生成では、3-wayを完全に網羅するために900件を超えるテストが必要である。埋め込みアサーション: ますます一般的になっている「軽量形式手法」の技法では、データ間の適切な関係を確保するために、コード内にアサーションを埋め込む。たとえば、事前条件、事後条件、入力値チェックとして使用できる。Java Modeling Language（JML）などのツールを使うと、非常に複雑なアサーションを導入し、実質的に形式仕様をコード内に埋め込める。埋め込みアサーションは仕様の実行可能な形式として機能し、試験段階のオラクルとなる。埋め込みアサーションを用いてアプリケーションをすべてのt-way組合せで実行すれば、非常に広範な入力にわたってコードが正しく動作するという合理的な保証が得られる。この方法はスマートカードの試験で成功裏に用いられ、埋め込みJMLアサーションが組合せテストのオラクルとして機能した [25]。その結果、この方法でエラーの80%～90%を検出できることが示された。

If a simulator can be used, expected results can be generated directly from the used, depending on simulation, but model checkers are widely available and can resources and the also be used to prove properties such as liveness in parallel system under test. processes, in addition to generating tests. Conceptually, a model checker can be viewed as exploring all states of a system model to determine if a property claimed in a specification statement is true. What makes a model checker particularly valuable is that if the claim is false, the model checker not only reports this, but also provides a “counterexample” showing how the claim can be shown false. If the claim is false, the model checker indicates this and provides a trace of parameter input values and states that will prove it is false. In effect this is a complete test case, i.e., a set of parameter values and expected result. It is then simple to map these values into complete test cases in the syntax needed for the system under test. Later chapters develop detailed procedures for applying each of these testing approaches.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 各入力の期待結果を生成する [1,8,9,52,55]。シミュレーターを使用できる場合、シミュレーションから期待結果を直接生成できるが、リソースや被試験システムによってはモデルチェッカーも使用できる。モデルチェッカーは広く利用可能であり、テスト生成に加えて、並行プロセスにおける活性などの特性を証明するためにも使える。概念的には、モデルチェッカーは、仕様文で主張された特性が真であるかを判断するため、システムモデルのすべての状態を探索するものと見なせる。モデルチェッカーが特に有用なのは、主張が偽の場合、その旨を報告するだけでなく、主張が偽であることを示す「反例」も提示する点である。主張が偽の場合、モデルチェッカーはその旨を示し、それが偽であることを証明するパラメーター入力値と状態のトレースを提示する。これは実質的に完全なテストケース、すなわちパラメーター値と期待結果の集合である。次に、これらの値を被試験システムに必要な構文の完全なテストケースへ簡単に対応付けられる。後続の章では、各試験方法の適用手順を詳述する。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Our task is to develop a covering array of tests for these inputs. The first step will be to develop a table of parameters and possible values, similar to that in Section 3.1 in the previous chapter. The only difference is that in this case we are dealing with input parameters rather than configuration options. For the most part, the task is simple: we just take the values directly from the specifications or code, as shown in Figure 10. Several parameters are boolean, and we will use 0 and 1 for false and true values respectively. For day of the week, there are only seven values, so these can all be used. However, hour of the day presents a problem. Recall that the number of tests generated for n parameters is proportional to vt, where v is the number of values and t is the interaction level (2-way to 6-way). For all boolean values and 4-way testing, therefore, the number of tests will be some multiple of 24. But consider what happens with a large number of possible values, such as 24 hours. The number of tests will be proportional to 244 = 331,736. For this example, time is given in minutes, which would obviously be completely intractable. Therefore, we must select representative values for the hour parameter. This problem occurs in all types of testing, not just with combinatorial methods, and good methods have been developed to deal with it. Most testers are already familiar with two of these: equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis. Additional background on these methods can be found in software testing texts such as Ammann and Offutt [2], Beizer [4], Copeland [21], Mathur [45], and Myers [52].

rebuilt_blocks.html: Practical testing often requires abstracting the possible values of a variable into a small set of equivalence classes. For example, if a variable is a 32-bit integer, it is clearly not possible to test the full range of values in +/- 231. This problem is not unique to combinatorial testing, but occurs in most test methodologies. Simple heuristics and engineering judgment are required to determine the appropriate portioning of values into equivalence classes, but once this is accomplished it is possible to generate covering arrays of a few hundred to a few thousand tests for many applications. The thoroughness of coverage will depend on resources and criticality of the application.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 実際のテストでは、変数が取り得る値を少数の同値クラスに抽象化する必要がある場合が多い。例えば、変数が32ビット整数の場合、+/- 231の全範囲をテストすることは明らかに不可能である。この問題は組合せテストに固有のものではなく、ほとんどのテスト手法で生じる。同値クラスに含める値の適切な範囲を判断するには、単純なヒューリスティックとエンジニアリング上の判断が必要となる。いったんこれを決定すれば、多くのアプリケーションについて数百から数千件のテストを含む被覆配列を生成できる。網羅性は、利用可能な資源とアプリケーションの重要度によって決まる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: In testing event-driven software, the critical condition for triggering failures often is whether or not a particular event has occurred prior to a second one, not necessarily if they are back to back. This situation reflects the fact that in many cases, a particular state must be reached before a particular failure can be triggered. For example, a failure might occur when connecting device A only if device B is already connected. The methods described in this chapter were developed to solve a real problem in interoperability test and evaluation, using combinatorial methods to provide efficient testing. Sequence covering arrays, as defined here, ensure that any t events will be tested in every possible t-way order.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Sequence covering arrays have been incorporated into operational testing for a mission-critical system that uses multiple devices with inputs and outputs to a laptop computer. The test procedure has 8 steps: boot system, open application, run scan, connect peripherals P-1 through P-5. It is expected that for some sequences, the system will not function properly, thus the order of connecting peripherals is a critical aspect of testing. In addition, there are constraints on the sequence of events: can't scan until the app is open; can't open app until system is booted. There are 40,320 permutations of 8 steps, but some are redundant (e.g., changing the order of peripherals connected before boot), and some are invalid (violates a constraint). 6 組合せ被覆率の測定

rebuilt_blocks.html: Since it is nearly always impossible to test all possible combinations, combinatorial testing is a reasonable alternative. For some value of t, testing all t-way interactions among n parameters will detect nearly all errors. It is possible that t = n, but recalling the empirical data on failures, we would expect t to be relatively small. Determining the level of input or configuration state space coverage can help in understanding the degree of risk that remains after testing. If 90% - 100% of the state space has been covered, then presumably the risk is small, but if coverage is much smaller, then the risk may be substantial. This chapter describes some measures of combinatorial coverage that can be helpful in estimating this risk that we have applied to tests for spacecraft software [50] but have general application to any combinatorial coverage problem.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 考えられるすべての組合せをテストすることはほぼ常に不可能であるため、組合せテストは妥当な代替手段となる。あるtの値について、n個のパラメーター間のすべてのt-way相互作用をテストすれば、ほぼすべての誤りを検出できる。t = nとなることもあり得るが、障害に関する実証データを踏まえると、tは比較的小さいと考えられる。入力または構成状態空間の網羅度を判断することで、テスト後にどの程度のリスクが残るかを理解しやすくなる。状態空間の90% - 100%が網羅されていればリスクは小さいと推測できるが、網羅率が大幅に低ければ、リスクは大きい可能性がある。本章では、宇宙機ソフトウェアのテストに適用した組合せ網羅率の測定方法[50]を説明する。これらの方法は、あらゆる組合せ網羅の問題に広く適用でき、残存リスクの推定に役立つ。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Of the total number of t-way combinations for a given collection of variables, what percentage will be covered by the test set? If the test set is a covering array, then coverage is 100%, by definition, but many test sets not based on covering arrays may still provide significant t-way coverage. If the test set is large, but not designed as a covering array, it is very possible that it provides 2-way coverage or better. For example, random input generation may have been used to produce the tests, and good branch or condition coverage may have been achieved. In addition to the structural coverage figure, for software assurance it would be helpful to know what percentage of 2-way, 3-way, etc. coverage has been obtained.

While this is not the same as a correctness proof, it is an effective way of integrating formal methods for correctness with program testing, and an extensive body of research has developed this idea for practical use (for a survey, see [4]). Some modern programming languages, such as Eiffel [52], include extensive support for including assertions that encode program properties, and tools such as the Java Modeling Language [42] have been designed to integrate assertions with testing. In many cases, using assertions to self-check important properties makes it practical to run thousands of tests in a fully automated fashion, so high-strength interactions of 4-way and above can be done in reasonable time.

To clarify this somewhat abstract discussion, we will analyze requirements for a small function that handles withdrawal processing for an automated teller machine (ATM). Graphical user interface code for the ATM will not be displayed, as this would vary considerably for different systems. The decision not to include GUI code in this example also illustrates a practical limitation of this type of testing: there are many potential sources of error in a software project, and testing may not deal with all of them at the same time. The GUI code may be analyzed separately, or a more complex verification with assertions may specify properties of the GUI calls, but in the end some human involvement is needed to ensure that the screen information is properly displayed. However, we can do very thorough testing of the most critical aspects of the withdrawal module.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Developing dependable software requires preventing as many bugs as possible and detecting, then repairing, those that remain. Testing can identify flaws in software, but after a failed test is discovered, it is necessary to determine what caused the failure. In most cases this may be accomplished for combinatorial testing in the same way as other test methodologies, using a debugger or in-circuit emulator. But one goal of combinatorial testing is to identify the particular t-way combination that triggered a failure. The problem of fault localization, identifying such combination(s), is an area of active research, but some basic approaches can be identified. The discussion in this chapter assumes systems are deterministic, such that a particular input always generates the same output.

rebuilt_blocks.html: At first glance, fault localization may not appear to be a difficult problem, and in many cases it will not be, but we want to automate the process as much as possible. To understand the size of the problem, consider a module that has 20 input parameters. A set of 3-way covering tests passes 100%, but several tests derived from a 4-way covering array result in failure. (Therefore, at least four parameter values are involved in triggering the failure. It is possible that a 5-way or higher combination caused the failure, since any set of t-way tests also includes (t+1)-way and higher strength combinations as well.) A test with 20 input parameters has C(20, 4) = 4,845 4-way combinations, yet presumably only one (or just a few) of these triggered the failure. To determine the combination at fault, a variety of strategies can be used.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Smart phones have become enormously popular because they combine communication capability with powerful graphical displays and processing capability. Literally tens of thousands of smart phone applications, or ‘apps’, are developed annually. Among the platforms for smart phone apps is the Android, which includes an open source development environment and specialized operating system. Android units contain a large number of configuration options that control the behavior of the device. Android apps must operate across a variety of hardware and software platforms, since not all products support the same options. For example, some smart phones may have a physical keyboard and others may present a soft keyboard using the touch sensitive screen. Keyboards may also be either only numeric with a few special keys, or a full typewriter keyboard. Depending on the state of the app and user choices, the keyboard may be visible or hidden. Ensuring that a particular app works across the enormous number of options is a significant challenge for developers. The extensive set of options makes it intractable to test all possible configurations, so combinatorial testing is a practical alternative.

rebuilt_blocks.html: As noted in the introduction, the key advantage of combinatorial testing derives from the fact that all, or nearly all, software failures appear to involve interactions of only a few parameters. Using combinatorial testing to select configurations can make testing more efficient, but it can be even more effective when used to select input parameter values. Testers traditionally develop scenarios of how an application will be used, then select inputs that will exercise each of the application features using representative values, normally supplemented with extreme values to test performance and reliability. The problem with this often ad hoc approach is that unusual combinations will usually be missed, so a system may pass all tests and work well under normal circumstances, but eventually encounter a combination of inputs that it fails to process correctly.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 序論で述べたとおり、組合せテストの主な利点は、ソフトウェア障害のすべて、またはほぼすべてが、わずか数個のパラメーターの相互作用に関係していると見られるという事実に由来する。構成の選択に組合せテストを用いるとテストの効率を高められるが、入力パラメーター値の選択に用いると、さらに効果的となり得る。テスターは従来、アプリケーションがどのように使われるかのシナリオを作成し、次に代表値を用いてアプリケーションの各機能を実行する入力を選択し、通常はこれに性能と信頼性を試すための極端な値を補う。場当たり的になりがちなこの方法の問題は、珍しい組合せが通常は見落とされることである。そのため、システムはすべてのテストに合格し、通常の状況では良好に動作しても、やがて正しく処理できない入力の組合せに遭遇することがある。

4.3 コストと実務上の考慮事項

rebuilt_blocks.html: Combinatorial methods can be highly effective and reduce the cost of testing substantially. For example, Justin Hunter has applied these methods to a wide variety of test problems and consistently found both lower cost and more rapid error detection [30]. But as with most aspects of engineering, tradeoffs must be considered. Among the most important is the question of when to stop testing, balancing the cost of testing against the risk of failing to discover additional failures. An extensive body of research has been devoted to this topic, and sophisticated models are available for determining when the cost of further testing will exceed the expected benefits [10, 45]. Existing models for when to stop testing can be applied to the combinatorial test approach also, but there is an additional consideration: What is the appropriate interaction strength to use in this type of testing?

rebuilt_blocks.html: Regular expressions are formal descriptions of strings of symbols, which may represent text, events, characters, or other objects. They are developed within automata theory and formal languages, where it is shown that there are direct mappings between expressions and automata to process them, and are encountered in many areas within computer science. In combinatorial testing they may be encountered in sequence covering or in processing test input or output. Implementations vary, but standard syntax is explained below.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 正規表現は、テキスト、イベント、文字、その他のオブジェクトを表す場合がある記号列の形式的記述である。正規表現はオートマトン理論と形式言語の分野で発展し、式とそれを処理するオートマトンとの間に直接的な対応があることが示されている。また、計算機科学の多くの分野で使われている。組合せテストでは、シーケンス網羅やテスト入力または出力の処理で使われる場合がある。実装によって違いはあるが、標準的な構文を以下に説明する。
